title: To Devs about Ai Slop Games.
author: 3xQuest
selftext:
Bros, if you're an actual pro game dev, you already know a couple of things.  
AI is a tool. It won't make you a finished game. There will be millions of projects started with it, and one in a million will actually ship. Same story as the hobbyist programmers who started making games years ago and never finished them. The ratio won't change. People will start games with AI, and nobody will finish them.  
I'm saying this as someone building a game right now. Not huge, not tiny, but we're doing it properly, clean and professional. And I can tell you: even with AI, it's tons of work. A full game, polished, bug-free — that's a serious grind. If you're really a dev, you know this.  
AI doesn't guarantee you a good game. It lowers the entry barrier, sure. Good games won't get any more common because of it. In a couple of months the platform will just learn to filter AI games — what's slop and what's a genuinely well-made one — and everything will settle.  
As for "the age of programmers is over" — yeah, agreed. People used to plow with horses, then they got tractors. It's just progress, and you deal with it.

Have fun and great success with your projects!

comments.body: the difference is, its way way easier to finish a game with AI, before AI I was finishing 1 in 5 or maybe 1 in 10 games I started. Today I can bring a game to a semi-polished state with all the features I want in 1 out of 2 games I started (the others I abandon as the gameplay does not make fun, not because I lost motivation on the game)

replies.author: 3xQuest
replies.body:
Fair — but you already knew how to finish games before AI. You had the skill. AI just made you faster.  
Look around: most people starting games with AI today have never finished anything. AI gets them to "semi-polished" faster — and that's exactly where projects die. Works for you, won't work for the crowd.

No, "discocovery" is purely in the hands of the dev and his marketing effort/quality. If before 10 out of 100 made that effort, now it's 10 out of 1000, it's still the same 10 Devs that will actually get all the sales in the end.

It doesn't matter how many games in total there are, the usual client sees a game being marketed and thinks "I want to play that" and then goes to find and buy it.

Only losers with no life "mindlessly browse" looking for games in a long list without even knowing what they are looking for.

Marketing is not putting out a demo on some specific day, it's not "posting once on Reddit", it's not "having a steam page". Very few put in the work required in to this, and that's why so few succeed. In the end, sales is everything.

It's a blessing to developers,
profile and stress test games without spending 2weeks building a detailed profiler 
Or 
Quickly resolve race conditions
Or
rendering to physic process profiling
Or 
Running 1000's of seeded profiled simulations to build analytics in order to make sensible value changes 
Or 
Deciding on optimization techniques 
By having ai use actual game data to determine the outcome of each possible method before you commit days worth of time doing the set ups to just revert back to the first optimization technique 


Above things 20% of it I couldn't even do prior ai (because it's just simply to much data to process when your logging physic ticks to find small out of place logs across 2minute+ analysis)
 
And the rest just simply ate up weeks of development time that sometimes even led to burnouts 

Ain't going back to that no sir
